dedupNotes: All 84 SAST findings are noise: SA-001..007 aderyn 'high' reentrancy = guarded nonReentrant CEI (migrators onlyOwner+nonReentrant, stakers contract-wide OZ ReentrancyGuard); SA-012/014/016-035 slither reentrancy-no-eth = same guarded CEI paths; SA-046..084 timestamp = masterchef time-comparison noise; SA-009..014/026/029/030 uninitialized-local = Solidity zero-init style; SA-015/028 incorrect-equality = view-only strict eq; SA-041/044 nonReentrant-not-first = CODE-002 false positive; SA-062/066/067 loop-cost/require-in-loop = gas/style. The four batchMint SAST items (SA-036 calls-loop, SA-037 reentrancy-events, SA-038 uninit, SA-039 unchecked-return) and SA-008 (unused-return configs) collapse into DEDUP-19-001 / and are the CODE-001/CODE-003 adjudicated non-bugs. No SAST finding survives as an independent candidate.

findings.oneLine: batchMint has no ReentrancyGuard and mints ERC1155 to a caller-chosen recipient mid-loop (onERC1155Received), but the snapshot-before-loop + nested forceApprove(minter,0) + post-loop pot transfer make every reentry self-defeating (reverts); no drain/theft. Recommend nonReentrant as DiD.
findings.resolution: NOT-EXPLOITABLE — self-defeating on every vector; Low defense-in-depth only
findings.ledgerCrossRef: L-01 (BatchNFTMinter no nonReentrant, submitted Low DiD)

findings.oneLine: emergencyWithdraw decrements totalStaked without a tail _recomputeSchedule, so in the APY model (R = S*APY/YEAR) survivors accrue at the pre-departure rate against a smaller pool until the next recompute-bearing interaction — bounded by rewardBudget, solvency-safe. Two hand-maintained copies (fork-drift), one class.
findings.resolution: Known M-02 class on both APY-model copies; Depletion copy affirmatively immune (rate is totalStaked-independent)
findings.ledgerCrossRef: M-02 (run-16) — owner-acknowledged WON'T-FIX (deployed + no migrate-on-behalf + pullAndRefresh mitigation); PriceScaled copy reconciles to same ack
findings.triageNote: Reconciles to M-02 won't-fix; sanitizer confirms PriceScaled fork-copy is covered by the same acknowledgement (WATCH-17 fork-drift).

findings.oneLine: Full nudgePaymentToken pot pays a caller-chosen recipient on a count-only gate (count >= nudgeSize), decoupled from contributed value; the minReward floor only protects the loser from paying, it does not bound/allocate the pot. Residual = MEV race to cross the threshold + owner over-funding footgun.
findings.resolution: Known lineage: H-01 (value-blind gate / fake-mint drain) fixed by story-014 minter-pin; M-01 (pot front-run) fixed via minReward; live residual = accepted MEV front-run + over-funding footgun
findings.ledgerCrossRef: H-01 fixed (story-014); M-01 fixed (minReward); L-05 (minReward==0 opt-out) won't-fix; LOCAL-BM-002 over-funding footgun accepted
findings.triageNote: Pattern-matcher rated potential-medium and explicitly says DO NOT auto-suppress — sanitizer must confirm the new minReward addition did not shift the accepted H-01/M-01 boundary before reconciling residual to Low.

findings.oneLine: Migrator stores stakedId as an immutable ctor param with no assertion it equals the staker's live stakedId; a legitimate setStakedId reconfiguration (NFT reissued under new ID) between deploy and use silently (1) kills the permissionless claimTimedOut escape hatch and (2) voids the parked-principal rescue floor (rescueERC1155 takes the else-branch, sweeps full balance with no totalParked guard).
findings.resolution: In-scope non-obvious footgun (Law 3); bounded to Low (no direct theft — rescue is onlyOwner)
findings.triageNote: Distinct contract from DEDUP-19-005 (parity-defeat with silent floor-void, vs dead immutable / clean-revert DoS). Keep separate.

findings.oneLine: NFTStakerMigrator stores an immutable stakedId that is NEVER referenced inside migrate() and never asserted equal across old/new stakers; a stakedId mismatch is a hard DoS with clean atomic rollback (no fund loss), and the unused immutable misleadingly implies a parity guarantee it does not enforce.
findings.resolution: QA/hardening — no value misrouted or stranded (clean revert-and-rollback)
findings.triageNote: Related to DEDUP-19-004 but distinct contract and distinct failure mode (clean DoS-revert here vs silent floor-void there). Keep separate per instruction.

findings.class: faithfulness — surviving unconditional window-restart on migrator path (M-01 window-restart CLASS)
findings.oneLine: story-020 removed the stake/unstake tail recompute (closing the permissionless M-01 rate-drift), but depositFor RETAINS an unconditional tail _recomputeSchedule that restarts windowEnd = now + windowSeconds on every call (both migrators loop it per-user). NOT the M-01 exploit (onlyMigrator, trusted, value-conserving, solvency-safe) — a faithfulness/operational residual; NatSpec 'for parity with stake' rationale is now false.
findings.resolution: Faithful-but-stale-rationale residual on the onlyMigrator path; same window-restart CLASS as M-01 but not the permissionless exploit — cross-ref M-01
findings.ledgerCrossRef: M-01 (fixed @321d0a9 in user paths; this is the surviving trusted-path window-restart, cross-ref only — not a reintroduction)
findings.triageNote: econ-scanner ECON-DEP-01 (below) confirms user-path M-01 restart is owner-accepted intended; F-01 is the migrator-path sibling. Confirm depositFor is not repeatably invocable to grief the window (onlyMigrator gate = no).

findings.oneLine: After story-020 the no-hook branch of _syncBudget settles accrual only (pure _updatePool) and no longer recomputes, but the NatSpec still says 'behaves like a pure recompute' — stale docstring. No functional impact (every config setter recomputes directly).

findings.class: operational footgun — dormant window after migration revive
findings.oneLine: finalizeAndReset revives a drained Migrating pool to Active but does NOT recompute the schedule; post-story-020 stake() no longer auto-rearms, so a revive-then-organic-stake sequence (no depositFor re-seed) emits nothing until the owner calls setDepletionWindow/topUp. Value never lost; emissions pause until re-arm. Intended consequence of story-020, surfaced as footgun.
findings.resolution: Low/operational; standard InPlace path self-heals via depositFor (which recomputes, F-01)
findings.triageNote: Borderline footgun (a frozen window is stale after any migration regardless); severity-classifier to confirm Low vs QA.

findings.oneLine: Immutable priceScale multiplies latestPrice with no upper bound beyond ctor !=0; a wrong magnitude (1e12 vs 1) swings emission rate/notional by orders of magnitude, and totalStaked*latestPrice overflow safety is only argued for priceScale <= 1e12. Non-obvious deploy footgun.
findings.resolution: Known L-08 footgun; do not re-escalate above Low
findings.triageNote: Matches L-08; sanitizer reconciles to ledger.

findings.oneLine: unstake does the outbound ERC1155 safeTransferFrom (onERC1155Received on caller-chosen recipient) BEFORE the tail _recomputeSchedule, so during the callback totalStaked is decremented while rewardRate/windowEnd still reflect the old pool — value-reporting views return a transiently inconsistent snapshot. State-changing reentry blocked by nonReentrant; impact requires an external oracle-style consumer of these views (none known in scope).
findings.resolution: Low / likely-informational — no known downstream integrator prices off these views mid-callback
findings.triageNote: Law 1 completeness — victim is a hypothetical downstream integrator, not this contract. Kept for triage rather than dropped; confirm no integrator reads staker views for collateral valuation.

findings.oneLine: DISPATCHER_INDEX hardcoded ASSUMED=4 and USDC hardcoded as nudge token; broadcast guards do NOT verify on-chain that the nudge token differs from the pinned dispatcher's primeToken() (only enforced at batchMint runtime). A wrong index pins the batcher to the wrong dispatcher/payment asset. Mitigated by documented manual-confirm + runtime revert.
findings.resolution: Operational/deploy hazard, not a contract bug — QA/triage

findings.oneLine: Every hook inflow>0 restarts the full depletion window (windowEnd = now + windowSeconds); a third party can force a restart by minting an NFT (permissionless) then calling claim(), lowering existing stakers' instantaneous rate. Self-defeating griefing: each restart costs a REAL paid mint whose mintDebt is donated into the budget and paid to the very victims; accrual settled at OLD rate first; solvency-safe; emissions deferred not destroyed.
findings.resolution: RECONCILED to M-01 — owner explicitly accepted restart-on-real-inflow as INTENDED (2026-06-25); NOT re-escalated. Listed for ledger traceability.
findings.triageNote: Kept as informational reconciled entry (not dropped) so the ledger sees the residual is accounted for; sanitizer reconciles to accepted M-01.
